newsitem.title: UK: British firework maker Astra defused by liquidator.
newsitem.headline: British firework maker Astra defused by liquidator.

text.p: British fireworks manufacturer Astra Fireworks is to be wound up, the liquidator to the firm said on Tuesday.
Accountancy firm Moores Rowland said Maurice Russell, an insolvency partner, had been appointed liquidator at a creditors' meeting in Walsall, central England.
Russell said Astra Fireworks had collapsed with debts of around 1.6 million ($2.6 million) pounds and because of the size of these debts it had not been possible to avoid liquidation.
Astra was taken over from parent group Astra Holdings in a 1990 management buy-out. It achieved an annual turnover of around 3.5 million pounds "before beginning to run into difficulties in 1995".
The full time staff of 16 had been laid off, while the rest of the workforce was employed on a seasonal basis.
"The fireworks sales season runs from September to November, and Astra had one bad season in 1995 and did not have the reserves to see it through," Russell said.
It had expanded its selling operation to include one of the major retail supermarket chains but this had proved unsuccessful and considerable stocks had been returned unsold.

"That involved incurring substantial reworking and repackaging costs. Things obviously did not go as well as the company had hoped. By the time it reverted to its old system of trading for the 1996 season, the damage had been done," Russell added.
